fact: The bright foot of the Twins, marking a brand on the sky.
bio: Alhena (Gamma Geminorum) is a blue-white subgiant about 109 light-years away, the third-brightest star in Gemini and set at the foot of the Twins near the edge of the Milky Way.
cultural: The name comes from an Arabic word for a brand or mark once made on the necks of camels. It sits close to the winter Milky Way, in the path the Sun, Moon and planets can occult.
